maya: Quick heads-up — on the canary fleet we pushed kernel selection tweak this morning and I’m seeing a perf spike for product-chat flows.
maya: KV cache hit-rate for RAG-style sessions fell from ~78% -> ~41% for a 30m window after the deploy :thinking_face:
liam: ugh. which tweak? kernel voting or batching window?
maya: kernel selection changed default to prefer kernel-quant-fast (v2.4.0-alpha) when seq_len>1024. batching coalescing window also bumped from 8ms -> 25ms in the same canary.
liam: could be the coalescing change — larger window can mix chat+RAG requests and change prefix alignment.
dan: do we have a quick telemetry diff per workload type (chat vs completion vs RAG)?
maya: pasted short query output: ```
-- telemetry summary (canary vs baseline)
workload    hitrate_before  hitrate_after  p95_lat_before  p95_lat_after
chat        0.81            0.78           56ms            62ms
completion  0.76            0.75           48ms            50ms
RAG         0.78            0.41           72ms            130ms
structured  0.83            0.60           60ms            110ms
```
maya: note structured = templates that start with JSON blocks + fixed system prefixes — seemed the worst multi-modal regression.
sasha: interesting. maybe kernel-quant-fast handles kv indices differently and our cache key canonicalization for JSON-ish prefixes mismatches? I remember earlier work on shingling keys for structured prompts.
dan: any sign of prefix canonicalization churn or fingerprint changes in logs?
maya: yes, found increased variance in prefix fingerprints: compare shard 3 from 10:02->10:20: ```
prefix_fingerprint_changes= true
unique_fps_before= 1.02M
unique_fps_after= 1.47M
most_common_prefix_share_before= 0.62
most_common_prefix_share_after= 0.37
```
liam: that’s huge. suggests previously-hot prefixes got split across fingerprints, reducing hit concentration.
infra-bot: Deploy 2034567000 rollback initiated for canary subset alpha-1
maya: thanks infra-bot. rollback scheduled. but we still need root cause — two hypotheses:
maya: 1) Larger coalescing window changes join semantics which affects how we build cache keys (we use a per-request convo hash + first-N tokens fingerprint; mixing requests changes token alignment and N selection).
maya: 2) Kernel selection path uses an optimized tokenizer variant for long context which normalizes whitespace differently -> different fingerprints.
sasha: for structured prompts we had a special shingle normalization that depended on whitespace normalization from tokenizer A. If kernel picks tokenizer B, we can break that invariant.
dan: can we reproduce locally by forcing kernel=kernel-quant-fast and coalescing=25ms on a controlled replay of RAG session logs?
liam: yes, I spun up a small canary with replay last night — saw same drop. I also captured a diff of computed cache keys for a sample conversation: ```
- key_old: conv_v2::sha1(\"user:search
ctx:block1
SYS:jsonstart\")
+ key_new: conv_v2::sha1(\"user:search
ctx:block1
SYS: jsonstart\")
```
liam: note the added space after SYS:. tiny whitespace shift.
sasha: that matches tokenizer change theory.
maya: plan: revert coalescing window to 8ms (already requested rollback). run two experiments: (A) kernel-selection pinned to previous tokenizer variant, (B) keep kernel but add canonicalization pass before fingerprinting that normalizes whitespace/shingles the same way across tokenizers.
dan: prioritize (B) in runtime — canonicalization is safer long-term. but we need quick mitigation too.
liam: for quick mitigation we can: 1) pin tokenizer selection in routing policy for RAG/structured routes, 2) add a short TTL bump to allow prefetched KV to re-warm (we can set TTL=30s -> 60s) so hit-rate recovers faster.
sasha: canonicalization checklist: normalize unicode, collapse repeated whitespace, remove punctuation in system markers, consistent lowercasing for keys that are not case sensitive, and stable shingle window of 16 tokens for structured prefixes.
maya: I’ll open an issue with a minimal repro + a small test harness that diffs keys between tokenizers.
infra-bot: Canary rollback completed for subset alpha-1 at 2034567920
liam: post-rollback telemetry looks better. initial 10-min window: RAG hitrate back up to 0.76, p95 down to 78ms.
maya: great. follow-ups: - implement canonicalization in runtime fingerprinting (sasha + dan) - add unit tests that run key-gen across tokenizers (liam) - update canary gating to include workload-specific cache hit-rate delta (prod-sre)
sasha: will draft PR for canonicalization today, include perf microbench to ensure we don't add +latency >1ms.
dan: I’ll add a regression test in e2e that replays 500 RAG sessions and asserts hit-rate remains within 5% of baseline after kernel changes.
maya: thanks team. notes and links: https://perf.redwood.internal/2034567890/session-prime-telemetry (private) and my repro gist: https://gist.github.com/maya/session-prime-diff
maya: closing thread for immediate ops — open new one for design discussion on long-term keying strategy later.
sasha: :thumbsup:
maya: 👍
